chunks: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his contracted slave-girl. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she had paid the quarter [of the manumission price], he would be whipped; and if he was married, he would be stoned; and if she had not paid anything, then there is nothing upon him [i.e., no hadd punishment].'

key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: His contracted slave-girl (who has a deed of manumission contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a man having intercourse with his contracted slave girl (mukatabah)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the hadd punishment for a master having intercourse with his mukatab slave-girl is contingent upon the slave's financial progress toward freedom, reflecting the principle that partial emancipation alters the legal status of the relationship. Specifically, if the slave has paid a quarter of the agreed price, the master receives flogging; if he is muhsan (married), he is stoned; but if no payment has been made, no hadd applies. This ruling highlights the dynamic nature of slavery in Shia jurisprudence, where the slave's economic agency directly influences the master's penal liability.

en.hubeali: Yunus, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who fell upon his contracted slave girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she has paid off the quarter (of what was owed by the contract), he would be whipped; and if he was married, he would be stoned; and if she has not paid off anything, so there is nothing upon him’.
